svg.title: Three character orbits over a regular nilpotent plane
svg.desc: E sends e3 to e1 to e2 to zero, E squared is q=E23, and E cubed is zero. The full normalizer sends E to aE+bq and q to a squared q. Its action on the character pair (u,v) has exactly three orbits, represented by (0,0), (1,0), and (0,1), with nilpotent sets of dimension two, a rank-one line, and a rank-two line. A separate coordinate exchange illustrates the discrete sign action on a diagonal-family scalar parameter.
svg.text: A normalizer shear removes a scalar coefficient
J₂ = ⟨E,q⟩, E = E₁₃+E₂₁, q = E² = E₂₃, E³ = 0.
e₃
e₁
e₂
E
E
E
The square q sends e₃ directly to e₂ and kills e₁,e₂.
Every normalizer action has this form, and every such action occurs
E ↦ aE+bq, q ↦ a²q, a ∈ ℂ*, b ∈ ℂ.
u = χ(E), v = χ(q) ⇒ v′ = v/a², u′ = u/a − bv/a³.
v ≠ 0: choose a²=v and b=u to obtain (u′,v′)=(0,1).
v = 0, u ≠ 0: choose a=u to obtain (1,0); zero remains zero.
⟨E,q⟩
Every matrix is nilpotent.
Nilpotent set: dimension 2.
⟨E+I,q⟩
Nilpotent set = ℂq.
Nonzero nilpotent rank: 1.
⟨E,q+I⟩
Nilpotent set = ℂE.
Nonzero nilpotent rank: 2.
An explicit conjugation, with no residual parameter
P = I+uE₂₁ ⇒ P(E+uI)P⁻¹ = E+u(q+I), P(q+I)P⁻¹ = q+I.
Thus ⟨E+uI,q+I⟩ is conjugate to ⟨E,q+I⟩ for every u ∈ ℂ.
The three cards are distinct by their nilpotent-set dimensions and ranks.
A disconnected normalizer can change an exact-looking scalar value
T₃(1,−1): exchanging e₁,e₂ sends D(1,−1) to −D(1,−1).
The identity matrix is fixed, so the graph parameter satisfies t ~ −t.
This is the full joint relation [1:−1:t] ~ [−1:1:t] = [1:−1:−t].
For the diagonal plane, all S₃ permutations of (α,β,−α−β) must be retained.
Proof: Theorem8.13, equations(8.39)–(8.40), Example8.14 and Solutions13–14.
Human source: Lie–Engel III, §29 pp.112–116, on character spaces and full normalizers.
All statements concern matrix conjugacy over ℂ; the complete arguments remain alongside the figure.
